title: Certificate request file (requests/<name>.json) read by the ca workflow
description: One file, one action. An issue request is written by the hub Worker when an admin approves a certificate request in the admin panel (approved_by, approved_at; the ca workflow fetches it by its id, see README "How a certificate is issued"), or by the CA operator by hand. woltrust's `wol cert request` makes the part from format to requested_at (woltrust::request::Request); the Worker adds id, subject.org, verified_at and the approval. An origin request needs cla_accepted_at and no approval; a trusted one needs approved_by and approved_at. A revoke for reason abuse needs two distinct approvers (ADR 0046).

id.description: The Worker's request id; the file is requests/<id>.json. Absent in a request the CA operator wrote by hand.

tier.description: Which certificate (lead decision 2026-11-04): origin = issued automatically once the CLA is accepted (cla_accepted_at; says who made a file and from which repository); trusted = a vetted developer or organisation, issued only with approved_by in CA_APPROVERS. A person or organisation may hold one active certificate of each tier. Named tier because kind (person|org) is covered by the proof.

org.description: Person only: the organisation the hub saw the person in (GitHub membership), copied into the certificate as subject.org.

subject.description: As the requester stated it. The certificate takes login and name from GitHub (by github_id) and org only when GitHub shows the membership publicly; a login that differs from GitHub's is refused.

requested_by.description: Who asked (the Worker's session). Organisation requests: must be an owner (admin) of the organisation, which the ca job checks with GitHub itself.

namespaces.description: Exactly the account's own prefix ["<login>."] (lowercase). The certificate gets the prefix derived from the login GitHub gives for github_id.

keys.description: Public keys, base64url without padding. x25519 and ml-kem-768 (encryption, wolos/seal/1) come both or not at all; the proof covers all of them.

verified_at.description: When the hub last verified the GitHub account; copied into the certificate (else the time of issue).

approved_by.description: GitHub logins of the hub admins who approved (never the subject); required for tier trusted.

cla_accepted_at.description: When the subject accepted the CLA (the Worker's record); required for tier origin.

serial.description: A certificate serial, or for reason withdrawn-version the statement serial of one listed version (index entry statement.serial).

approved_by.description: GitHub logins of the hub admins who approved (never the subject).

at.description: Ignored: the ca job uses its own clock for the revocation time (audit-1 M4).
